title: AI-MARRVEL random forest improves diagnosis of Mendelian disorders in three cohorts
summary: AI-MARRVEL, a random forest classifier trained on over 3.5 million variants from diagnosed cases, was benchmarked on three independent real-world cohorts. The abstract reports that it doubled the number of solved cases compared with benchmarked methods, reached 98% precision while identifying 57% of diagnosable cases among 871 cases, and correctly predicted two newly reported disease genes from the Undiagnosed Diseases Network. The evaluation is retrospective benchmarking.
ai_technology: Random forest classifier (AI-MARRVEL) trained on over 3.5 million variants
organization: Baylor College of Medicine; Texas Children's Hospital

evidence.tested: Diagnostic yield compared with benchmarked methods in three cohorts, a confidence metric on 871 cases, and prediction of two newly reported disease genes.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective benchmark; prospective clinical effect not shown; full text not reviewed.
